about: Graph changes that the node specs ask for in prose, plus the plan assembler's and plan fixer's resolution of conflicting requests. build_app_plan.py applies these on top of final-graph.json (the 23 Sep graph data) AFTER it has read the structured fields of every node note (frontmatter title, milestone, oracle and human_gate, the first range on the Estimate line, the wikilinks on the Depends on and Unlocks lines, and the Owned paths section). Each entry names the note and line it comes from. Edges are written dependency -> dependent. Assembled by Opus 5.5 on 24 Sep 2026 and revised the same day by the plan fixer after the independent review; the independent reviewer checks this file with the plan.
streams_note: Three parallel build streams, the limit A01 freezes ('up to three nodes may build at once'). Four streams are shown for comparison only; using them needs an A01 change first.

AM0.goal: Charter and coverage baseline (91 screens, 22 journeys including the D04 journey J22, 22 gates, 27 modules, 14 state machines), git repo and pinned toolchain, pure domain package (integer money, unit math, ids, all 14 state machines, permission matrix, gate codes incl. G22), Postgres schema with RLS, design system generated from the dc prototype tokens, local Hardhat chain with T-REX vendored, sandbox adapter framework, API and worker skeleton with the OpenAPI-generated SDK (the seed and scenario simulator A06 moved to AM1, because it seeds token, audit and session rows from A10, A11 and A12). Exit: `npm run verify` passes on a fresh clone on Node 24.21.0 and the T-REX reference suite compiles and tests green locally.
AM0.exit: none (A05, A07, A08 and A09 close it)

AM1.goal: The risk core, proven before any UI: append-only audit chain, passkey/hardware-key auth with RBAC and SoD, API tokens with agent mandates for every user type (G22) and the MCP server generated from the OpenAPI document, the seed and scenario simulator, the alerts and SLA-clock service, approvals engine (SM-00) with custody policy sandbox and approval-ID binding, double-entry client-money ledger, NPP/PayID bank rail sandbox, the legal unit register with registry adapter, the rules engine for G01-G22, three-way reconciliation with zero tolerance, licence-bound feature flags, identity and sanctions sandboxes, and A12's follow-up loop A12.1 (approval-backed token routes). Exit: the whole stack (postgres, api, worker, hardhat, sandbox panels) boots green from Docker Desktop three times in a row, migrates, seeds, deploys the reference suite and the audit chain verifies; no live adapter or mainnet RPC is selectable.

AM2.goal: ERC-3643 suite per trust with RealX compliance modules, the AgentGateway that binds approval IDs on-chain, passkey smart wallets with paymaster and guardian recovery, chain adapter and indexer feeding reconciliation, token operations service, wallet service; and design extension A (A50: the undrawn and partly drawn investor, public, sponsor and partner screens and the drawn-screen supplements), moved here from AM4 on 24 Sep 2026 so that its build uses idle streams and the user's HG-REVIEW of it happens while the backend is built. Exit: a mint bound to an approval id runs approval to custody to gateway to indexer to registry ack to a clean targeted reconciliation on the local chain, and a replayed approval id is refused at every layer.
AM2.exit: none (A28, A29 and A50 close it; A50 holds its dependents until the user's HG-REVIEW, which may be given while AM3 runs)

AM3.goal: Every API module the screens will need, each tested against the core and publishing its read contracts into the SDK: KYC and onboarding cases, on-chain claims, classification, tenancy and entities, properties and valuations, documents, offerings, orders/escrow/allocation, finalise-and-mint pipeline, treasury, distributions, tax, AML, comms, support, reporting, jobs, portfolio read models, halts and wind-down, partner principals, the IAM admin API for ADM-37 (A106) and the agent guard (anomalies, notices, tiered kill switches). Exit: the money-path smoke runs J04, J05, J06 and J15 at service level through the SDK and sandbox panels in Docker (pay in, close, allocate, register entry, mint, reconcile, distribute, withdraw) and the founder can watch money and units move from a one-page 'magic inputs' guide.

AM4.name: Design extension, shells and developer surface
AM4.goal: Design extension B (A51: the undesigned operator console screens, incl. ADM-35 and the five undrawn admin screens renumbered ADM-36..ADM-40, and their drawn-screen supplements) drawn in the prototype's own language and reviewed by the user before any console node uses it (extension A, A50, with ACC-05, SPN-16 and the PUB-05 standalone page, moved to AM2 on 24 Sep 2026); the web app shells (public, investor, sponsor) with passkey sign-in and the operator console shell with hardware-key sign-in; and the developer surface (API versioning, reference docs, per-user sandbox, SDK and MCP packaging; A99, moved from AM3 so that A49 closes AM3). Exit: the user has reviewed extension B in the browser and approved it (human gate HG-REVIEW), and extension A's HG-REVIEW from AM2 is recorded.
AM4.exit: none (A51 to A53 and A99 close it)

AM5.goal: Public site, onboarding, buy flow, portfolio, wallet, account and the investor and sponsor API-token screens on top of the proven services, then a Docker Desktop preview the user can open, re-run in full once every AM5 screen node has passed (A61.1). Exit: J01, J02 and J04-to-escrow pass as Playwright journeys over the preview stack, A61.1 has captured every AM5 screen including ACC-05, and the user has walked the preview (human step).

AM8.goal: Playwright journeys J01-J06, J09-J15, J17, J19-J21 with planted breaks, the D04 journey J22 driven by an agent through the API/MCP and the agent-parity matrix, security and performance passes, observability and runbooks with the nine runbook drills executed, backups with a restore drill and retention/erasure, a Base Sepolia integration run with the HG-AUDIT pack, design fidelity and accessibility, three clean regression runs with every gate G01-G22 exercised, and the Docker Desktop launch. Exit: all 18 P1 journeys (17 product-map journeys plus J22) green three times in a row and the P1 software sign-off (HG-LAUNCH-P1-LOCAL) recorded by the user; HG-LAUNCH itself stays open for go-live.

loop_allowance.note: Planning allowance per follow-up loop run that has no estimate of its own. A loop runs once per (loop id, requester) pair, because the orchestration keys a follow-up by the loop id and the requesting node (status id '<AXX.n>-<requester>'): a second requester of the same loop id gets its own run with its own change list, even after the first has passed. Each pair is counted in the milestone of its requester (a loop that only its owner names counts once, in the owner's milestone). Pairs whose requester carries the loop hours on its own Estimate line are not counted again, and a citation that only names a loop as a pattern ('the pattern A12 used for A04.1') is not a request. Unnumbered mentions (AXX.x, AXX.n) carry no allowance, because the Specify step gives them a number first.

Interface-only edges on the critical path (A12 -> A06, A06 -> A13, A20 -> A27, A28 -> A35, A28 and A29 -> A43) are kept. The orchestration runs one milestone at a time, so an edge between milestones never lengthens the run; the two inside AM1 (A12 -> A06, A06 -> A13) carry real seed data (token rows, the design's alerts) that A06 and A13 need at their gates. Replacing them with recorded fakes is left to the reviewer.
resolved_items: 24 Sep 2026, plan fixer: the oracle flags that notes required in prose are set in the notes' frontmatter: A98, A93 and A59 (their text already required the Oracle stage), A46 and A53 (decided as oracle nodes under D04's 'oracles where money or authority is involved'; reversible by a one-line frontmatter change). A check_plan.py rule now fails when a note's body requires the Oracle stage while its frontmatter says `oracle: no`.
docker_challenge_share_note: Share of each Docker-using node's estimate that is its stack-bound Challenge and re-verify work. The orchestration serialises those steps with one Docker lock across the streams (every worktree has its own compose project name, but all stacks bind the same host ports, so only one runs at a time), so the barrier and overlap schedules run this share one node at a time. A node uses Docker unless its lane is Plan, Domain core or Design, it is A01, or its frontmatter says `docker: no`. A planning assumption, re-measured after AM0.
